subject: Private connectivity decision criteria, requested port list & allowlist
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@netfin.com>, NetFin Cloud Ops <cloudops@netfin.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private connectivity decision criteria, requested port list & allowlist

Hi Alicia / NetFin Cloud Ops team —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and request list so we can size the Private VPC path and confirm timelines: 

Recap (what we heard)
- NetFin: must keep model inference and customer inputs off the public internet for regulated workloads.
- Preferred outcome: Private connectivity (private endpoint) rather than hosted public API.
- Compliance ask: audit trail + tenant isolation; ownership of egress allowlist is important.

Open items / asks from Redwood to proceed with a formal Private VPC proposal
1) Preferred connectivity method: PrivateLink endpoint or VPC Peering? (We recommended PrivateLink for cross-account isolation; see notes below.)
2) Egress allowlist: please confirm the team that will own allowlisting and share any existing production NAT egress IPs you want Redwood to whitelist for callbacks/health checks.
3) Port / protocol list: please provide the ops firewall port list we should expect to open on your side. If you don’t have that yet, we’ll propose a minimal port set.
4) Pilot/test CIDR: a small /28 that we can use for initial connectivity testing (if applicable).

Redwood technical notes (high level)
- PrivateLink is our default recommendation for customers who want strong account-level isolation and simpler routing (no cross-account route table changes).
- VPC Peering is an option for teams that prefer direct L3 connectivity and control over entire route tables, but it requires more coordination with your networking and NATs.
- For allowlists: even with PrivateLink, outbound egress from our infra (for metrics, telemetry, or webhook callbacks) may come from a small set of public IPs that we can provide.

Attachments: redwood-postcall-checklist.pdf — contains our recommended pilot steps and timelines.

Next steps we propose:
- You confirm preferred connectivity model and point people for netops.
- NetFin shares preliminary allowlist IPs (or confirms that Redwood should provide our egress IPs to be whitelisted).
- Ben (cc’d) will follow up with the minimal port/protocol proposal for PrivateLink.

I’ll hold a 30-min follow-up if helpful once we have the port list. Proposed window: Tue/Wed afternoon.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@netfin.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: NetFin Cloud Ops <cloudops@netfin.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private connectivity decision criteria, requested port list & allowlist

Jonas —

Appreciate the clear recap. We are leaning strongly toward Private VPC with PrivateLink because our security team prefers endpoint-based models for third-party vendors. A couple quick answers and follow ups from our side: 

- Connectivity preference: PrivateLink (subject to Cloud Ops confirmation).
- Owning team for allowlist: NetFin Security will sign off, but NetFin Cloud Ops will manage the ACL entries. I’ve looped cloudops.
- Preliminary NAT egress ranges (for our outbound systems) — see attached network diagram for context; we don’t yet have the final prod egress IPs to give you for inbound allowlisting. Cloud Ops, can you provide the expected NAT egress IPs for dev/test and prod?

We also have one compliance question: where is TLS terminated in Redwood’s topology for PrivateLink? Is Redwood terminating TLS at the endpoint or will TLS be end-to-end to our backend? Security needs that clarified for our PCI/PII scope.

I’m available Tue 10:00–11:30 ET for a short follow-up.

Thanks,
Alicia Ramos
Director, Security Programs — NetFin
alicia.ramos@netfin.com | +1 212-555-4444

Attachments: netfin-network-diagram.png (referenced)

---
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@netfin.com>, NetFin Cloud Ops <cloudops@netfin.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private connectivity decision criteria, requested port list & allowlist

Hi Alicia / Cloud Ops —

Thanks for the quick reply. I’m Ben (solutions architect) — looping in Marissa from our delivery team. Short technical answers and a minimal port list to get a PrivateLink pilot standing up: 

PrivateLink vs VPC Peering — quick pros/cons- PrivateLink: endpoint service, no route table surgery on your side, recommended for multi-tenant cloud accounts and when you want vendor-level isolation.- VPC Peering: straight L3, lower latency, but requires managing routes/NATs and potential IP overlap handling.

Minimal ports/protocols we need open from your side (PrivateLink pilot):
- 443 TCP (HTTPS) — primary API traffic (required)
- 443 TCP — mutual TLS to webhook endpoints (if you have callbacks)
- 5228-5230 TCP (optional) — health and metrics proxies if you opt into our metrics pipeline (we can make this optional in pilot)
- 22 TCP (SSH) — only for scheduled debug sessions into a maintenance bastion (requires preapproval; we prefer to avoid)

Allowlist guidance (what we need from you vs what Redwood provides)
- For PrivateLink, the interface endpoint is inside your VPC so ingress is internal. However, some Redwood control-plane operations and telemetry may originate from a fixed set of public egress IPs. If you need complete lock-down, we can provide the egress IPs for test and prod.
- Please share NAT egress IPs for any private subnets that will call Redwood services so we can confirm match and avoid asymmetric firewall drops.

Proposed test/prod egress IPs we can offer to allowlist (example ranges; final values to be sent after we create the tenant):
- Test: 52.17.200.128/28
- Prod: 52.17.201.0/28

Pilot runbook (high level)
1) Cloud Ops creates PrivateLink endpoint and shares endpoint ID.
2) NetFin allowlists Redwood egress (or we confirm PrivateLink-only flow).
3) Redwood runs connectivity checks and posts health results.
4) 24–48 hour pilot with synthetic load to validate latency and SLOs.

I attached a simple diagram and will follow up with a short checklist (I’ve included redwood-postcall-checklist.pdf in Jonas’s original mail).

Let me know if the port list looks OK or if NetFin wants to tighten before pilot.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0124

Attachment: netfin-network-diagram.png (annotated)

From: Alicia Ramos <alicia.ramos@netfin.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: NetFin Cloud Ops <cloudops@netfin.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 08:31:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Private connectivity decision criteria, requested port list & allowlist

Ben / Jonas —

Thanks — that port list helps. A couple clarifications before we lock pilot dates: 
- TLS termination: Security confirms we need end-to-end TLS to our backend (Redwood should not terminate TLS in a way that inspects payload). Can you confirm Redwood supports mTLS passthrough to customer-hosted endpoints in PrivateLink mode?
- Regarding your example egress blocks: please mark those as provisional. Cloud Ops, can you confirm our actual NAT egress blocks for dev/test by EOD? Prod will take longer.

We can do the pilot window Wed 28 Apr 14:00–17:00 ET if you can support that. Otherwise we’ll pick next week.

Alicia

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private connectivity decision criteria, requested port list & allowlist

Alicia / Cloud Ops —

Short answers and next steps: 
- mTLS passthrough: yes — Redwood supports end-to-end TLS passthrough for PrivateLink so TLS is terminated at your backend. We will not perform payload inspection unless you opt in to advanced telemetry. I’ll get a short technical note from our infra team and share it in a follow-up.
- Pilot window: Wed 28 Apr 14:00 ET — Ben and I will be available for the pilot. We’ll treat the example egress blocks as provisional until Cloud Ops confirms.

Action items (owners)
- NetFin Cloud Ops: confirm dev/test NAT egress IPs and share prod ETA (cloudops@netfin.com).
- NetFin Security (Alicia): confirm that mTLS passthrough satisfies compliance; we’ll provide the infra note for audit.
- Redwood (Ben): finalize the port list and provide the tenant egress IPs (final ranges once tenant is provisioned).
- Redwood (Jonas/Marissa): send a short SOW/Docusign link for the pilot scope and timeline so NetFin can approve and we can schedule delivery.

Doc links: HubSpot record and a Drive folder where we’ll drop the SOW/infra note.

I’ll send the DocuSign link within 24 hours. Looking forward to the pilot.

Best,
Jonas
